side_a: CC 3.3.1: `consent:state:*` rows on one subject use the same boundary fold, the latest admitted revocation's `asserted_at` putting every earlier grant out
side_b: CC 4.4.3.5.5: a revoke is terminal for the grant it names (its supersedes_id); a revoke that
note: CC 3.3.1 puts every grant at or before the latest revocation out, whichever row it named; the CC 4.4.3.5.5 read path removes only the named or withdrawn grant, so an older unnamed grant resolves to granted. Withdrawing the newest grant resurrects an older one under 4.4.3.5.5 and never under 3.3.1. The consent model pinned by the register follows CC 3.3.1.

side_a: CC 3.3.1: the agent key's withdrawal is folded like the owner's, a boundary `R`
side_b: CC 3.3.1: A grant or revocation from a key that was neither the node nor its owner at the row's `asserted_at` is not this node's consent and MUST NOT be folded
note: Same registry cell. The agent key is the third named party and its withdrawal is a boundary; the closing rule folds a revocation only from the node or its owner. One reading stops capture on the agent key's withdrawal, the other ignores it. The four readings (later text, pinned model) support folding it; the closing sentence wants "or a party the grant names".

side_a: CC 3.1.1: Entity revocation (`agent` / `partner` / `license`). Immediate, non-rollbackable.
side_b: CC 2.4.1.1: An occurrence revocation, a key grant and a cosignature already sent are never withdrawn either
note: CC 3.1.1 makes an entity revocation non-rollbackable, and CC 2.4.1.1 cites that very cell as the reason a key:revocation is never withdrawn; yet the never-withdrawn list omits revocation:{entity_type}:{reason}, rule 1 admits its signer's withdraws with no condition, and family_model.json and transitions.json give withdraw to the attester. Whether an authority can take back a licence or agent revocation differs by the statement read.

side_a: CC 2.4.1.1: A node MUST admit a `withdraws` against a target row `T` when one line of this table holds.
side_b: CC 3.3.6: an eviction is a `withdraws` against the `identity_occurrence` row, proposed by a live roster key and landing under [CC 3.3.6.3](#3.3.6.3)
note: An occurrence row is single-signer (CC 2.4), so rule 1 admits its signer's withdraws at once with condition none; CC 3.3.6 makes the same withdraws a proposal that lands only by the quorum or lone path. CC 2.4.1.1 does not list the exception. Same shape as C344 (owner-binding gate): the specific home governs; family_model notes it. The home table should cite it.

side_a: CC 3.3.6: an eviction is a `withdraws` against the `identity_occurrence` row
side_b: CC 3.3.6.3: the genesis key's eviction is an `identity_occurrence` revocation of the pair (fedID, fedID) signed by another live roster key
note: Two wire shapes named for one act: a withdraws row against the occurrence (CC 3.3.6, CC 3.4.4) and an occurrence revocation, the framed SignedIdentityOccurrenceRevocation carried by identity:occurrence_revocation (CC 3.3.6.3, CC 3.1.3), which is never withdrawn. side_b: manifests/transitions.json: membership:{stage} withdraw roles member, policy cosigned

side_a: CC 3.4.13: their signature no longer counts toward any prior co-signed widening. If their departure breaks the authorising quorum, that scope auto-narrows to the floor.
side_b: CC 2.4: **Retraction of a cosigned row is by the same quorum**
note: A guardian's own withdrawal un-counts a signature on an admitted cosigned widening, where CC 2.4 and rule 0 let only the quorum undo it and CC 2.4.1.1 says acts taken stand. C010 settles it as a stated default-revert exception for a minor; both wordings are unchanged.

side_a: CC 3.3.4: A widening or removal is judged at its signed instant, which its signers choose.
side_b: CC 4.4.3.4.2: current = resolve_family(F, now)
note: CC 2.4 and CC 3.3.4 judge a cosigned roster event on the fold at its signed instant, a departed signer counting inside W; the CC 4.4.3.4.2 gate resolves the roster and counts signatures (and the founder role) against the roster at now. A signer who left between signing and receipt counts under one and not the other, so the same event is admitted or refused. CC 2.6.7 and the membership model support the signed instant.

side_b: CC 4.4.3.4.2.1: under which a halt fires on the live set and a roster change counts its yes-votes against the standing roster
note: CC 4.2.6 and CC 4.2.1.1 fire the halt on one holder's row with no live set and no count; the closing sentence of CC 4.4.3.4.2.1 still has the halt fire on the live set (so does the CC 3.2 T7 aside "with a live set and a floor-of-1 fire"). Stale wording; CC 4.2.6 is the home.

side_a: CC 2.4: served to the group's active members only, for the hold window of [CC 3.3.4](part_3_the_namespace.md)
side_b: CC 3.3.4: served to the members who were active at the event's signed instant and are members still, and to no one else
note: CC 2.4 serves a held change to every active member; CC 3.3.4 and the CC 3.1.3 row serve only those active at the signed instant and still members, so a member seated after the event was signed is served under one and not the other. Such a member cannot sign the event either way; the narrower rule is the home.

side_a: CC 2.4.1.2.1: A `licensure:{community_key_id}` row is a **cosigned row** ([CC 2.4](#2.4)) whose protocol source is the authority named in the dimension.
side_b: manifests/family_model.json: licensure:{authority_id} cosign_rule "none" (code-v61); transitions.json attest registered, policy selfAct; withdraw author, selfAct
note: The text makes an organisation-named licence a cosigned row under the affiliation's protocol (CC 3.3.9: a signature set short of it MUST NOT issue one), withdrawn only under rule 0. The data and the CC 8.10 card admit any registered single signer and let the author withdraw alone, with no branch for an organisation authority. The card is normative where it states a value, so the two cannot both be followed.

side_a: CC 3.3.4: the accord-holder family per [CC 4.2](part_4_composition_governance.md) decides by a strict majority of its standing roster
side_b: CC 5.3.4: It finishes at **M distinct holder authorizations** (the charter's `quorum:2/3`
note: The accord family's protocol is named `majority` (entrenched) in CC 3.3.4 and the charter's `quorum:2/3` in CC 5.3.4; under absolute M the two diverge once the roster grows, which CC 5.3.4 patches with max(M, strict majority). The CC 3.1.3 rebind row says only "the accord charter's threshold". C040 settled it for the standing-roster majority; the 2/3 wording is still in CC 5.3.4.

side_a: CC 5.3.3.6: For accountable streams, "published" means **witness-cosigned** (the CC 5.3.1 path), so the subscriber cannot collude with the producer on a private root.
side_b: CC 8.10: attest: `one transparency_log:cosigned:{tree_size}@admitted[val:log_id=leaf:stream_id,val:root_hash=val:chunk_root,leaf:tree_size>=val:K] else refuse` (CC 5.3.3.6)
note: The text asks a witness-cosigned root only of an accountable stream; a best-effort stream publishes a producer-signed root and its witness cosign is optional (CC 5.3.3.3). The delivery_receipt guard in transitions.json and its CC 8.10 card refuses every receipt with no admitted transparency_log:cosigned row, so a node built from the card refuses receipts on best-effort streams the text admits.

side_a: CC 2.4: transparency-log heads and cosigns ([CC 5.3.1](part_5_transport_substrate.md) framing)
side_b: CC 3.1.2: Witness cosignature on an STH (substrate-conformance path; see [CC 5.3.1](part_5_transport_substrate.md) endpoints). Witness-emitted, verify-recognized
note: CC 2.4 lists log heads and their cosigns as off the plane, not claims; CC 3.1.2 registers transparency_log:cosigned:{tree_size} as a family of rows with a reserved emitter (CC 3.4.10), and the delivery_receipt guard reads such rows. A reader cannot tell whether a witness cosign is a framed object only, or also a row. CC 3.4.10 says the lineage-head cosign is "not an attestation row"; nothing says so for the STH cosign.

side_a: CC 3.1.2: emitter rule (`identity_type="witness"`) at CC 3.4.9
side_b: CC 3.4.10: `transparency_log:cosigned:*` is reserved: emitter rule is `attesting_key_id` MUST match a `federation_keys` row with `identity_type="witness"`
note: Citation: the CC 3.1.2 registry row and the CC 3.4.5 log-infrastructure bullet send the reader to CC 3.4.9 (co-stewarded prefixes) for the witness emitter rule; the rule is CC 3.4.10, which CC 3.2 T6 cites correctly.

side_a: CC 3.2: A cosignature on a head is verified against the directory of that head's **parent**, and the genesis head against the bundle's charter.
side_b: CC 5.3.1: against the witness's key record in the **charter's** witness directory for that lineage (never a directory of its own)
note: CC 3.2 T6 and CC 5.3.4 verify a lineage cosignature against the parent head's directory, never the head's own charter; the Registry route in CC 5.3.1 says only "the charter's" directory. On a head that changes the directory, a Registry reading CC 5.3.1 alone may count the new directory's witnesses. CC 3.2 is the home.

side_a: CC 2.6.5: Certificate Transparency v2.0 (CT-bis); MUST be used for new transparency-log integrations; older 6962 instances continue to interoperate
side_b: CC 5.3.3.3: `root_hash` is the [RFC 6962](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc6962) Merkle root over the first `tree_size` leaves
note: CC 2.6.5 makes RFC 9162 mandatory for new log integrations; the stream log (CC 5.3.3.3, CC 5.3.3.7), the cosign request (CC 5.3.1.1) and the CC 3.1.2 rows name RFC 6962. CC 2.6.1.8 notes the tree hashing is the same, so roots agree; the proof and structure formats named differ.

side_a: CC 3.3.6: An `identity_occurrence` row is signed by a live roster key of the identity (the genesis key or any admitted occurrence) and lands under the two-path policy
side_b: CC 4.5.12.3: A new `identity_occurrence` is admitted on a signature from EITHER the root `identity_key_id` (until the self evicts its genesis key) OR any currently active occurrence of that identity
note: CC 3.3.6 lands every occurrence admission by the two paths (majority at once, or the lone path after 86 400 s); CC 4.5.12.3 is headed single-vouch, admits on one signature, and its rationale rejects multi-vouch, then sends a user-role key to the roster door. Read whole, 4.5.12.3 splits by role; CC 3.3.6 states no split. CC 3.3.6.3 and the self_roster policy rows are the home.

side_a: CC 3.3.1: Lapse of a grant when `valid_until` passes without renewal.
side_b: CC 3.3.1: which it emits for a lapsed grant (`expires_at`, or a `retain:<window>` in the scope) with `consent_supersedes` naming the grant
note: Two cells of one table name different members whose passing lapses a grant: valid_until (also CC 3.3.5, CC 4.4.3.5.5, reactions.json) against the row's expires_at or a retain window in the scope. CC 2.1 holds valid_until and expires_at independent. A grant carrying only one of them lapses under one reading and not the other. The read path also names the link `supersedes_id` where this cell says `consent_supersedes`.

side_a: CC 4.2.1.3: A **confirmed** halt carries no TTL: expiry would convert the brake into a wait-out for the halted party
side_b: CC 8.10: expiry required `valid_until` max `accord_heartbeat_max_secs` (CC 3.4.1)
note: reactions.json and the CC 8.10 card put the heartbeat's required valid_until (at most 90 days, then read stale) on accord:lifecycle:{kind}, the confirmed and active rows. CC 3.4.1 gives that cadence to the heartbeat accord:lifecycle:v1, "a different row", and CC 4.2.1.3 gives a confirmed halt no TTL. A node built from the card ages a confirmed halt out; the heartbeat family accord:lifecycle has no expiry entry.

side_a: CC 3.2: The ≤ 90-day refresh cadence of `accord:lifecycle:active` is not a validity leg either
side_b: CC 3.4.1: `accord:lifecycle:active` is the resumption kind, a different row
note: CC 3.2 T4 gives the 90-day refresh cadence to accord:lifecycle:active; CC 3.4.1 and CC 3.1.1 give it to the heartbeat accord:lifecycle:v1 and make active the resumption after a halt. The T4 wording is the stale name and is the likely source of the misplaced expiry entry in reactions.json.

side_a: CC 4.2.6: within `halt_fuse_secs` of the halt, or the lone halt lapses
side_b: CC 4.2.1.1: The fuse is counted from receipt on the node's own clock, never from the signer-chosen `asserted_at`.
note: The CC 4.2.6 table measures the confirmation "of the halt" with no instant named; CC 4.2.1.1 runs the fuse from each node's own receipt. C039 settled it for per-node receipt and reactions.json follows (from first_held, by receipt); the table wording is unchanged.

side_a: CC 2.4.1: `delegation_valid_until` is **REQUIRED, at most 365 days (365 × 86 400 s) after `delegation_valid_from`**
side_b: CC 3.4.12: delegates_to.valid_until <= T2_review_cadence
note: The envelope member of a delegates_to edge is delegation_valid_until (CC 2.4.1, CC 2.6.1.7); the CC 3.4.12 predicate requires `delegates_to.valid_until`, and valid_until is a different member with a consumer-staleness meaning (CC 2.1). A reader of 3.4.12 alone may gate on the wrong member. CC 3.4.13 uses delegation_valid_until.
